clue.text: Edward the First interrupted work of a patricide

indicators.note: the shorter pieces break into the middle of the word for a composition, cutting it open

parts.note: an opus is a musical or literary work
Ed is the usual short form of the name Edward
I is the Roman numeral for one, as in a regnal title such as Edward I

explanation.surface: A history note: a medieval king barging in on a play about a man who killed his father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edward the First' reads as one king, but splits into ED and I.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend this king of Thebes unknowingly killed his father Laius, making him the classic father-slayer.

clue.text: Religious devotee died but not in time

parts.note: ob. is short for Latin obiit, he or she died, seen on gravestones
late means not on time

explanation.surface: A pious believer died, though not in good time.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblate is a layperson dedicated to religious life, often attached to a monastery.

clue.text: Fond of a spot in government

parts.note: a dot is a spot

explanation.surface: Someone loves a beauty spot in government land.
explanation.definitionFit: Doting means excessively loving, an intensified form of being fond.

clue.text: Fairy meets goddess in place that's unimportant

parts.note: a peri is a fairy in Persian myth

indicators.note: the goddess sits inside the abbreviation for place

parts.note: Pl. is the abbreviation for place in addresses
Hera is the Greek queen of the gods

explanation.surface: A fairy and a goddess meet in some minor, out-of-the-way spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Peripheral things sit on the edge rather than the centre, hence minor or of little significance.

clue.text: Lustre noticed when touring hotel

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the word for observed goes around the hotel letter

parts.note: seen means noticed
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A traveller notices the gleam of a hotel while touring.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheen and lustre both mean a soft shine on a surface.

clue.text: One remains in bed, being embarrassed

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, meaning one

indicators.note: the word for what remains after burning sits within the word for a place to sleep

parts.note: taken as written
ash is what remains after a fire

explanation.surface: Someone stays under the covers, too mortified to get up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' looks like a verb (stays) but is the noun for leftovers after burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Abashed describes the state of feeling shy and ashamed, a synonym phrase for being embarrassed.

clue.text: Winger in a last-minute switch

indicators.note: the bird goes inside the word for tardy

parts.note: late means at the last minute
a winger is anything with wings, here the seabird tern

explanation.surface: A football winger is brought on as a late substitution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer but is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To alternate is to switch back and forth between two things.

clue.text: Top copy marked with a kiss

parts.note: to ape is to copy
X represents a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: The best copy of a document is signed with a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or summit of something.

clue.text: Number taken in by flighty female is to increase

indicators.note: the number is held within the bird word

parts.note: a hen is a female bird, flighty because birds fly
eight is a number

explanation.surface: A capricious woman is fooled by a figure that promises growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests deceived; here it means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To heighten is to raise or intensify something, a synonym of increase.

clue.text: Began turning up carrying cargo, initially of spoils

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the cargo's opening letter inside it
in a down clue, turning up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: started means began

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word next to it

explanation.surface: A ship began to arrive with cargo, some of it spoils of war.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that detracts from a thing spoils or diminishes it.

clue.text: Broke bread in both hands in time

indicators.note: the eating is held between the two hand letters

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right
to break bread is to eat a meal, so here it means ate

explanation.surface: Someone tears a loaf apart with both hands, just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke bread' is an idiom for having eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens later comes in due course, after a while, which is what 'in time' means.

clue.text: Fanatic makes setter mix cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixed blend, so the letters of these words are shaken together into a new order

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler shakes up a drink so wild only a zealot would order it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mix' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'cocktail' does the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanatic and an extremist are both people holding views far beyond the moderate mainstream.

clue.text: Can first ones in get kitchen utensils?

parts.note: a can is a tin
the first people in, who open proceedings, are openers, as in cricket batsmen opening an innings

explanation.surface: A queue question: can the first ones through the door grab the cooking gear?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' reads as a verb asking permission but is the noun for a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: These devices for cutting open sealed metal food containers are standard kitchen tools.

clue.text: Bird featured in banner headline

indicators.note: the answer appears as letters running within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A newspaper puts a bird story on its front page under a banner headline.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird, related to the ostrich.

clue.text: Cope with Spike's perspective

parts.note: to stand something is to cope with it
a spike is a point

explanation.surface: A view on how to handle someone named Spike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike' looks like a name; it is a sharp point.
explanation.definitionFit: A standpoint is the position from which one views matters, a point of view.

clue.text: Sing to fellows in hospital department in delight

indicators.note: the singing and the men are placed inside the letters for the hospital unit

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
to chant is to sing
fellows are men

explanation.surface: Singing to the patients and staff of a hospital ward brings them joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Enchantment is a state of great pleasure or captivation, a synonym of delight.

clue.text: Help senior officer to function

parts.note: CO is a Commanding Officer
to operate is to function

explanation.surface: A senior officer is asked to assist and get things working.
explanation.definitionFit: To cooperate is to work together and assist, so it fits help.

clue.text: Patronage put life into Australia

indicators.note: the word for life is put inside the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: spice is used to mean life or zest, as in 'variety is the spice of life'

explanation.surface: A sponsor injects new energy into Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the auspices of someone means under their sponsorship or protection.

clue.text: Filter surprisingly isn't rare

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests letters in an unexpected order, so these are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised that a filter is a common item.
explanation.definitionFit: A strainer is a sieve-like device that filters solids out of a liquid.

clue.text: Ruler to damn building that's avant-garde

indicators.note: building means constructing, so the letters of these words are assembled into a new form

explanation.surface: A monarch condemns a new building as too experimental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like a noun for the structure condemned, but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both terms describe something extremely new and experimental in style, ahead of current fashion.

clue.text: Lion-tamer is an idle outcast

indicators.note: outcast means cast out or thrown about, so these letters are scattered into new order

explanation.surface: A circus lion-tamer has been fired for laziness.
explanation.walkthrough: The biblical prophet survived the lions' den, so he is a jokey lion-tamer.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Daniel the prophet is thrown to lions which do not harm him, as if tamed.

clue.text: Trojan bully

definitions.meaning: the Trojan prince and greatest warrior of Troy in the Iliad

explanation.definitionFit: The name of Troy's champion is also a verb meaning to bully, after the swaggering stage version of him.

clue.text: Fruit and veg recipe

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable
R is the abbreviation for recipe (Latin recipe, 'take'), as on a prescription

explanation.surface: A cookbook entry for a fruit-and-vegetable dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The pear is a common orchard fruit, so the definition names the class it belongs to.

clue.text: Wrap instrument and start to hand through the window

parts.note: a cello is a stringed musical instrument

indicators.note: the opening letter passes into the glass piece, sitting inside it

parts.note: a pane is the glass of a window

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone wraps a cello and passes it out through the window.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellophane is a thin transparent film used as a wrapping for food and gifts.

clue.text: Mark's punishment

definitions.meaning: marks drawn on a page, such as strokes
a school penalty of copying out a sentence many times

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both strokes drawn on a surface and the old school punishment of repeated sentences.

clue.text: Overcome by today's leader in newspaper

indicators.note: the leading letter sits inside the newspaper's name

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone is stunned by the lead story in the day's paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' hints at a newspaper editorial, but picks the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to shock or daze them, leaving them overcome.

clue.text: Force prisoners to study

parts.note: cons is slang for convicts
to train is to study for a skill or job

explanation.surface: Inmates are compelled to take up education.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain someone is to compel or restrict them, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Number one detective books clown

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
DI is a Detective Inspector
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: The top detective arrests a clown.
explanation.definitionFit: A clown, in the sense of a fool or buffoon, is someone behaving stupidly.

clue.text: Road rage grips Pole? That's awkward!

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a road

indicators.note: the anger word holds the pole letter inside it

parts.note: taken as written
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A furious driver grabs a Polish man in a road-rage incident, an uncomfortable scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a Polish person; it is a magnetic pole, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange can mean uncomfortable or ill at ease, as when someone feels out of place.

clue.text: Gun dog bites hand of pioneer

indicators.note: the dog's name closes around the hand letter as if holding it in its jaws

parts.note: a setter is a dog used in shooting to point out game
L stands for left, as in left hand

explanation.surface: A hunting dog nips the hand of a frontiersman.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler is one of the first people to make a home in new territory, like a pioneer.
